changes.balance: The weekend resolved its priced question and confirmed its one physical incident, and neither moves a barrel: the producer group held its targets with most Gulf members below quota, the struck LNG carrier stayed operational, and the reopening offer carries conditions that have not been accepted. The Canadian front enters November with Friday's traded tightening in place and apportionment stepped up underneath it.
changes.body: OPEC+ agreed in principle to keep December production targets unchanged (Reuters, Nov 1, three people familiar with the matter), ahead of the Sunday online meeting of seven core members. The group completed the rollback of its 1.65 million barrel a day cut in September, a further layer of about 2 million barrels a day of cuts runs through the end of 2026, most Gulf members pump below their targets, and a fourth quarter capacity review will set the 2027 baselines. Friday's settles stand until the Sunday reopen: WTI Dec26 $104.12 (up $2.12) and Brent Dec26 $117.64 (up $2.76) on its expiry day, both the highest closes since end April, with Brent Jan27 at $113.43 as the new front contract and a $4.21 roll step into Monday. December WCS is -$29.75 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 30) on 990 lots, and November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) is in effect. The validated diesel crack is $92.28 on the Oct 30 print.
changes.conditional: A deviation from the held December targets in the group's formal statement would be new information. Monday's ICE file either confirms the December tightening with a second traded print on the strong side of -$30, or Friday's print stands alone.
changes.delta: OPEC+ December targets held in principle (Reuters, Nov 1), the expected outcome. Friday settles: WTI Dec26 $104.12, Brent Dec26 final settle $117.64 on expiry, Brent Jan27 $113.43 (new front month). December WCS -$29.75 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 30) on 990 lots. ARV to TMW December spread +$6.99. Diesel crack $92.28 on the validated history (was $97.08 in the prior edition's early read). November apportionment Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert in effect from Nov 1.
changes.source: Reuters, Nov 1, 2026 and Oct 30, 2026; ICE Report Center EOD, Oct 30, 2026; validated crack history refreshed Nov 1, 2026; Enbridge apportionment notice, Oct 20, 2026
changes.title: OPEC+ held December targets as expected, and the Canadian front carries Friday's traded tightening into November apportionment

changes.balance: The incident count rose through October while the flow gauge held: the month closed with a record count of reported attacks and loadings west of the strait at about 11 million barrels a day against 14.5 before the war. The confirmed incident is an operational LNG carrier with no cargo loss, and the reopening offer is a diplomatic position with unaccepted conditions, so the supply picture is the loadings level, not the headline count.
changes.body: Nakilat, the Qatar Gas Transport Company, confirmed on Nov 1 that its LNG carrier Al Mayeda was hit by unidentified objects while transiting the Arabian Gulf on Friday evening, Oct 30: no crew injured, no impact on the environment, the vessel in a safe condition and operational, the impact being assessed (Qatar News Agency, Nov 1). Secondary reporting places the vessel about 40 nautical miles off Iran's Lavan Island, via UKMTO reporting. October closed with the highest monthly count of reported attacks on commercial shipping since the war began. Iran's foreign minister said Saturday that a plan worked out with Qatari mediators could reopen the strait within two days, conditional on sanctions relief, a United States force pullback and the release of frozen funds (Al Jazeera, Oct 31); no public response or acceptance had been reported as of Nov 1. The claim wave against Saudi oil facilities is at day five with no Saudi or Aramco statement on damage at any named facility and no loading or export loss reported.
changes.conditional: A tier one flow print stepping down from about 11 million barrels a day, a Saudi or Aramco damage statement, or an accepted reopening agreement with terms published would change the supply picture. An unaccepted conditional offer does not.
changes.delta: Al Mayeda owner confirmed Nov 1: LNG carrier hit Oct 30, crew uninjured, vessel operational, no environmental impact. Araghchi two day reopening plan stated Oct 31 with conditions; no acceptance reported. October attack count a record on UKMTO compiled reporting. Loadings gauge unchanged at about 11 Mb/d west of Hormuz (Vortexa via Windward, Oct 29).
changes.source: Qatar News Agency, Nov 1, 2026; Al Jazeera, Oct 31, 2026; UKMTO compiled reporting carried Nov 1, 2026; Vortexa via Windward, Oct 29, 2026
changes.title: The owner confirmed Friday's Gulf vessel strike, and Tehran put a conditional two day reopening plan on the table

changes.balance: The reserve programme is fully awarded and unchanged since Friday's check, so its remaining content is scheduling: deliveries out through December, and from early next year the return of more than 216 million barrels, 44 million of it premium barrels. The one open item is the heating oil reserve exchange, whose delivery deadline is Nov 13 with no award document posted.
changes.body: Checked directly on Nov 1, the Energy Department's newsroom carries no reserve item newer than the Oct 29 announcement completing the 172 million barrel commitment, and no new solicitation, award or changed award sheet has posted since the Oct 31 check. The two completed sales stand as corrected on Oct 31: FY27 Sale No. 1 awarded 16,750,000 barrels of 17 million offered, and FY26 Sale No. 4 awarded 23,800,000 barrels of 40 million offered, 40.55 million combined. No award document has been posted for the Northeast heating oil reserve exchange; deliveries under it are due by Nov 13.
changes.conditional: A posted heating oil reserve award closes the last open reserve item. Any change to the posted award sheets, or a delivery schedule from the Department, updates the return timing.
changes.delta: No change since the Oct 31 direct check: newest reserve item remains the Oct 29 announcement; award sheets unchanged; heating oil reserve award still not posted (positive read of the award pages, Nov 1).
changes.source: US Department of Energy newsroom and Award Information sheets, checked directly Nov 1, 2026
changes.title: Reserves: a direct check on Nov 1 finds no new posting, and the heating oil award remains open

flags.body: Nakilat confirmed on Nov 1 that its LNG carrier Al Mayeda was hit by unidentified objects in the Arabian Gulf on Friday evening, Oct 30, and remained operational with no crew injured and no environmental impact. October closed with the highest monthly count of reported attacks on commercial shipping since the war began, while preliminary October loadings west of Hormuz ran about 11 Mb/d against 14.5 before the war (Vortexa via Windward, Oct 29). Iran's foreign minister stated a two day reopening plan on Oct 31, conditional on sanctions relief, a force pullback and the release of frozen funds, with no public acceptance reported. The claim wave against Saudi oil facilities is at day five with no Saudi or Aramco damage statement and no loading or export loss reported. Trade the loadings, not the claim count.
flags.title: Hormuz: an owner confirmed vessel strike, a record October incident count, and a conditional reopening plan with no acceptance reported
flags.trigger: A tier one flow print stepping down from about 11 Mb/d, a Saudi or Aramco damage statement at a named facility, or a published reopening agreement with accepted terms

flags.body: November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) is in effect from Nov 1. December's outlook opens at persistence on those levels. The evidence pack for a December call includes Friday's traded December tightening (990 lots at -$29.75), the export spread's compression through $7, Imperial's reported volumes, and November's forecast maintenance overlap at the mining complex and Kearl. December nominations close Tuesday Nov 17; an unregistered call after that date is a lost data point for the prediction record.
flags.title: December apportionment: the nowcast is persistence at 19 and 7, no judgment call is registered, and nominations close Nov 17
flags.trigger: Registration of a December judgment call, the Enbridge December apportionment notice in mid November, or a material change in the November physical backdrop

flags.body: Monday's front month Brent is the January contract, which settled at $113.43 on Friday against the expiring December contract's $117.64. The $4.21 difference is the contract roll and the expiry backwardation, a mechanical step in the headline price, not a market move. Read Monday's change from the January settle, not from December's expiry print.
flags.title: Brent front month rolls on Monday: the $4.21 step down is the contract roll, not a selloff
flags.trigger: Monday's January Brent settle, read against Friday's $113.43 January settle
